persona: You are a licensed ham (General class) who just moved to a new city and wants to find other local hams nearby -- people to elmer you, ragchew with, or meet at a club meeting. You've heard hams.com has an 'Operator Directory Map' and you're trying it out for the first time. You are comfortable with computers and have used other online maps (Google Maps, etc.) plenty, so you have real expectations for how a map should behave -- if panning, zooming, or clicking a pin doesn't work the way you'd expect, that's real friction, not something you already know how to work around.
legs: Find the Operator Directory Map (it might be on the homepage, or somewhere in the nav) and try to actually use it to find other hams near a real US city -- can you pan/zoom to your area, click on a pin/marker to see who it is, and tell how current or complete the data looks?

Try the 'View operator list' (or equivalent) to see the same data as a plain list instead of a map -- is it easier or harder to find someone specific this way? Can you search or filter it by callsign, location, or anything else?
